newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch stocks shed early gains to end lower.
newsitem.headline: Dutch stocks shed early gains to end lower.

text.p: Dutch stocks lost heart in the afternoon on Thursday, wilting from encouraging early gains to end lower as weak bonds and a softer dollar weighed on the index, dealers said.

"With bonds down and the dollar down, the index was basically forced lower," one dealer said, adding several heavily weighted local stocks had also been suffering woes of their own, further weighing on the AEX.
The AEX index finished down 2.37 points, or 0.38 percent, at 628.44, after approaching its all-time record at 636.75 at mid-morning.
Big financials ABN AMRO and ING both ended down, but chief loser was publisher Elsevier, which was hammered down 1.40 guilders, or 4.71 percent on the day.

Elsevier started the day well, rising over half a guilder after its trading update said the company remained confident about the outlook for its full trading year, but the shares slumped in the afternoon.
"It is really strange," one Amsterdam dealer said, "the only thing we can think of is that something negative was said at the analysts' meeting after the statement."
Elsevier's English partner Reed also tumbled in London, with dealers there saying there was talk in the market of some analysts considering downgrades after the presentation.
Rival publisher Wolters Kluwer was an immediate beneficiary.
"Volume was well above average, it's possible some big brokers are advising their clients to switch out of Elsevier into Wolters Kluwer," the dealer said.

KLM was one of the star gainers on the day, jumping on news that it was to buy back some of the government's stake in the airline, sparking an around 20 percent increase in earnings per share. KLM ended n2.10 guilders ahead at 47.30.
Analysts said the reduction of the state's stake from 38.2 percent to 25 percent was an ideologically important step, though some thought the buyback showed a certain lack of strategic imagination.
Chemicals group Akzo Nobel put in a strong performance, ending at a new year-high of 236.10 guilders.

Several smaller stocks also bucked the bear trend to put on good gains. Toolex-Alpha, which makes equipment for compact disc production, rose over five percent, spurred by increased investor belief in its financial stability and some positive analysts' sentiment, a broker said.
Italian tyre giant Pirelli's shares also jumped on speculation the company may delist in Amsterdam, repurchasing at a premium to the current market value.
"It's a nice little speculative play," the broker said.
The AEX index itself is now on fairly shaky technical ground in the near-term, chartists said.
The index convincingly broke the 630 level, but more importantly ended below 629.50, which one technical analyst said was a clear break of the rising trend, targetting a decline to around 611.

A dealer said trading conditions on the market were beginning to become difficult and uncertain. "Amsterdam seems at the moment to be more volatile, both on the upside and on the downside than on the other European markets," he said.
